headline: NEUTRAL
headline_tag: A month of losses; the last weeks still lean down

action.title: HOLD at planned level
action.detail: Keep marketing and acquisition budgets at the planned level, but do not step them up: Bitcoin is down about 9% in a week and about 26% in a month, a Rally watch drop window has been open since 13 November, and the headline could turn BEARISH within days if the weakness lasts. Keep a reserve ready instead of cutting, because the long-run base is still rising; spend now on retention, trust and education, and step up acquisition only once price closes back above the 200-week average ($68,246) and then the 200-day average ($72,551). This is a budget posture, not trading advice.

reasons: Price is about 20% under its 50-day average, 30 days in a row.
Down about 26% over 30 days and about 19% over 90 days.
Fear & Greed is 12 (extreme fear); price is about 9% under its 200-week average.
The 200-day average ($72,551) is still rising, about 5% over 90 days.
watch: The headline still says NEUTRAL, but the medium-term reading has been in its weak zone for three days and would turn the headline BEARISH if it stays there two more days. A close back above $64,000 and then $68,246 (the 200-week average) would be the first sign the drop is easing; a close below $60,000 would deepen it.
analysis: Bottom line: Bitcoin is still under pressure in a very fearful market, so today stays about holding steady, safety and education, not promotions. Short term, the picture is soft: at about $62,104 Bitcoin has closed under its 50-day average for 30 days in a row, sits about 20% below it and about 24% under its 30-day high, and Fear & Greed reads 12 out of 100. News is pulling this a little lower, as PANews reports the wallet behind October's Binance theft moved about $248 million of ETH to new wallets and swapped some of it into BTC. A normal week lately swings about $3,971, so a close above $64,000 (the top of a typical week's swing) would turn the week up, a close below $60,000 (the bottom of it) would turn it down further, and in between it stays choppy; calm safety and explainer messages fit far better than offers.

The next month leans down: the medium-term reading has now been in its weak zone for three days, and if it stays there two more days the headline would switch from NEUTRAL to BEARISH, while the long-term trend is still up. Price is about 26% lower than 30 days ago and about 19% lower than 90 days ago, and US spot Bitcoin funds lost about $487 million on the latest day. Bitcoin would have to win back $77,703 (the 50-day average) before the month can firm up, and only above $86,603 (the 90-day high) is there real room to climb. The Fed meeting on 8 December is the next scheduled event, and JPMorgan now expects a rate rise there (via PANews); keep bigger campaign pushes until after a clear turn.

The 3-6 month picture still leans up, but only just: the 200-day average is still rising (about 5% over 90 days), yet price is about 14% under it, about 9% under its 200-week average and about 50% below its all-time high. News is adding a little here, as PANews reports Russia's central bank plans to let funds for qualified investors buy crypto and UBS is moving structured notes onto a blockchain with Chainlink. The recovery is only back on track if Bitcoin closes above $72,551 (the 200-day average) again; $68,246 (the 200-week average) is the floor price has slipped under, and $124,753 (the all-time high) stays the far marker. More weeks under the 200-week average would turn this picture down and be the time to shift budget toward keeping existing users.

items.theme: Anthropic's IPO arrives on crypto exchanges as tokenized stock
items.why: PANews reports Anthropic opened at $111.50 on Nasdaq, about 34% above its $83 IPO price, and Coinbase, Binance, Kraken, OKX, Bybit and Robinhood's chain all listed tokenized or regular versions on day one. Binance Wallet says it could not get the shares it wanted, so it is refunding about 500 million USDC of subscriptions and adding a $1 million token airdrop.
items.marketing_angle: A clear education moment: what a tokenized stock is, how it differs from owning the share, and why exchanges are adding them.

items.theme: Regulators turn to on-chain trading platforms like Hyperliquid
items.why: PANews reports the US CFTC chair said on-chain platforms that want to serve US retail users must get their own license or work with a licensed exchange, and Hong Kong's SFC put 'Hyperliquid/Hyperliquid Hong Kong' on its list of suspicious unlicensed platforms. At the same time 1inch launched trading built on Hyperliquid.
items.marketing_angle: A good moment to explain why licensed, local exchanges matter, without naming or criticising other platforms.

sources.title: CFTC Chair: Hyperliquid and Other Onchain Platforms Need Their Own License or a Licensed Partner to Serve US Retail
Hong Kong SFC Flags "Hyperliquid/Hyperliquid Hong Kong" as Suspicious Virtual Asset Trading Platform
